description: Fires on moves with significant eval loss. Severity tier + side-specific framing + a concrete WHY clause when the extractor produced one. Suppression block keeps the rule from saying anything when we have no concrete fact AND the loss isn't blunder-tier.

fact_glossary.best_move_san: Engine's preferred move (when different from played)
fact_glossary.severity_phrase: Authored phrase ('is a mistake' / 'is a serious mistake' / 'is a major blunder') — picked from severity_phrases by severity_tiers
fact_glossary.why_clause: Optional appended sentence — Python pre-renders the why_clauses_user/opp entry that matches, sets facts['why_clause'] before evaluating select_variant
fact_glossary.moving_piece_type: Type of the piece that just moved
fact_glossary.opp_reply_san: Opponent's strongest reply (PV[0] after the played move)
fact_glossary.captured_piece_type: Piece type the opponent's reply would capture
fact_glossary.user_best_reply_san: User's strongest reply after an opp blunder
fact_glossary.missed_tactic_kind: Climax of pv_after_best — 'mate' | 'piece_capture' | 'material' | absent. Set by best_move_tactic_detector by walking the engine's recommended line and finding the tactical payoff (mate / wins a piece / wins pawns).
fact_glossary.missed_tactic_target_piece: When missed_tactic_kind = piece_capture: the piece type won (e.g. 'queen', 'rook').
fact_glossary.missed_tactic_target_square: When missed_tactic_kind = piece_capture: the square on which the piece was won.
fact_glossary.missed_tactic_ply: When missed_tactic_kind = mate: number of plies in the PV to checkmate.
fact_glossary.shape_pattern_id: Geometric pattern fired on the pre-move board (e.g. 'king_pawn_lifted', 'h7_attack', 'pin'). Set by V5 service before render via shape_layer.select_shape_for_position.
fact_glossary.shape_pattern_target_square: Square the shape pattern is centered on (e.g. 'f7' for a king_pawn_lifted on Black's f7).
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_attack_square: Square that the engine's best move would have opened up for attack via clearance (Légal's / Fried Liver family). Set by V5 service when simulate_clearance_for_attack(best_move) fires on the pre-move position.
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_attacker_piece: Lowercase piece name (queen / rook / bishop) of the slider whose line would have been opened by best_move. Used by the missed_clearance_attack why-clause to name the piece in coach voice instead of internal 'slider' jargon.
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_then_check_piece: Lowercase piece name (queen / rook / bishop) of the slider that would have given check after the best move's clearance — Légal's-Mate family. 2-move plan: best_move opens the line, the named slider plays a check on the next move. v56 (2026-05-22) — fix to v53's overcorrection that dropped 2-move detection entirely; see memory/feedback_fix_framing_not_detection.
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_then_check_destination: Square the slider moves to after the best move's clearance to deliver the check (e.g. 'h5' for Qh5+).
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_then_check_follow_up_sa: Hand-built SAN of the slider's check move (e.g. 'Qh5+'). Computed by detect_clearance_then_check via a null-move push to flip turn before board.san().
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_then_check_king_square: Square of the king being chased (e.g. 'e8'). Names the target plainly in the caption.
fact_glossary.attack_with_tempo_piece: Lowercase piece-name (queen/rook/bishop/knight/pawn) the engine's best move attacks, where opp's PV[1] retreats THAT piece. v57 (2026-05-22) — captures the 'with tempo' tactical pattern from Mohit's approved captions #1 (Qe2/d4 hits bishop on c5) and #2 (e4/Nh4 hits bishop on f5). Excludes king (checks are a different family — queen-fork pattern).
fact_glossary.attack_with_tempo_square: Square where the attacked piece sat (e.g. 'c5'). Used by the why_user_missed_attack_with_tempo template to name the target plainly.
fact_glossary.attack_with_tempo_follow_up_san: SAN of the engine's PV[2] move — what white plays AFTER opp retreats the attacked piece. Often a capture (Bxf4, Bxb7) that defines the tactical payoff. Optional; when absent the template just names the tempo attack without the follow-up.
fact_glossary.queen_fork_sub_kind: 'capture_with_check' (queen captured a piece on its destination AND gives check) or 'fork' (queen moves to a square attacking king + another undefended opp piece). v61 (2026-05-22) — Mohit approvals #5 (Qb3+), #16 (Qh4+), #19 (Qxb4+).
fact_glossary.queen_fork_secondary_piece: Lowercase piece name of the captured/forked target (the non-king target).
fact_glossary.queen_fork_king_square: Square of the opp king under check.
fact_glossary.endgame_loose_pawn_sub_kind: 'direct_capture' (best move IS the capture, e.g. Kxh3) or 'attack' (best move attacks the pawn, e.g. Rf3 → next Rxh3). v62 (2026-05-22) — Mohit approvals #13, #15.
fact_glossary.endgame_loose_pawn_moving_piece: Lowercase piece-name doing the grabbing (king / rook / bishop / knight / queen).
fact_glossary.endgame_loose_pawn_square: Square of the loose (undefended) opp pawn.
fact_glossary.position_was_already_losing: true when the user's eval has been losing (<= -150cp from user POV) for the last 3+ user moves before this one. Tells the caption to frame the move as 'damage control' rather than 'source of the loss' — the real problem is earlier in the game.
fact_glossary.losing_since_move: Earliest move number in the contiguous losing run. Used by the with-known variant to point the user back at where the position started going wrong.
fact_glossary.piece_type: Piece-type generic placeholder used by hanging-piece why-clauses
fact_glossary.square: Square placeholder used by hanging-piece why-clauses
fact_glossary.mover_is_user: true if the mover is the user
fact_glossary.opp_reply_attacks_played_piece: true when opp's PV[0] directly attacks the just-moved piece
fact_glossary.is_exchange_losing: true when the move itself landed on a losing-exchange square
fact_glossary.pieces_now_undefended_present: true when at least one own piece is now undefended (set by Python from the pieces_now_undefended list)
fact_glossary.opp_pieces_now_undefended_present: true when at least one opp piece is now undefended after their blunder
fact_glossary.opp_played_landed_unsafe: true when opp's move stranded their own piece
fact_glossary.best_move_san_differs: true when best_move_san is present AND != played_san
fact_glossary.opp_reply_san_is_check: true when opp's PV[0] ends with '+' or '#'
fact_glossary.user_best_reply_san_is_forcing: true when user_best_reply_san ends with '+' or '#'
fact_glossary.curriculum_deviation_clause: Hand-authored wrong_feedback from opening_curriculum.json — the tree's teaching for the deviation the user just played. Set by V5 service when get_opening_guidance reports is_in_book=True with expected_move ≠ played_san. Priority above generic blocked_pawn / board_state detectors but below concrete-about-played-move clauses (hanging, capture, check, exchange_losing) so a tactical 1-move blunder still wins over book-theory teaching.
fact_glossary.curriculum_expected_move: The book-theory move the tree expected the user to play (set alongside curriculum_deviation_clause).
fact_glossary.curriculum_opening_name: The matched opening's position_name from the curriculum.
fact_glossary.user_is_winning: true when user_eval_after >= +200cp from user POV. Triggers user_winning_position variant for cp_loss < 250 with no why_clause — reframes 'X is a mistake' as 'X is fine, you're still winning' (per Mohit 2026-05-21: when up by a queen, no positional move should be labeled 'a mistake' — it's misleading coaching).
fact_glossary.user_is_losing: true when user_eval_after <= -200cp. Triggers user_losing_position — reframes as context ('you were already losing') instead of blame.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_file: File letter ('a'..'h') of a user pawn whose advance was blocked by the played piece move. Set by principle_blocked_pawn detector when the engine's best move was a pawn move to square X and the user played a non-pawn piece to X. Fires the why_user_blocks_own_pawn variant — names the opening principle the user just violated (don't block your own central pawn support).
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_square: The target square (e.g. 'c3') the user's pawn would have moved to.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_would_support: The first central-pawn square (e.g. 'd4') the user's pawn would have supported diagonally. Only set when the pawn would have supported a real central pawn — gives the why-clause its specific teaching value.
fact_glossary.board_state_clause: Pre-rendered 1-3 sentence string describing the post-move board state from user's POV (Mohit 2026-05-21). Composed in Python by board_state_describer: pick top 3 facts (with diversity across categories), render each from a bs_* template, join with '. '. Fires as why-clause when nothing more specific did — universal fallback that stays in coach voice rather than engine-speak.
fact_glossary.bs_piece: Piece type placeholder for individual bs_* templates (e.g. 'knight')
fact_glossary.bs_square: Square placeholder for individual bs_* templates (e.g. 'e5')
fact_glossary.bs_user_developed: Count of user minor pieces developed (off home squares) — used by bs_development_gap
fact_glossary.bs_opp_developed: Count of opp minor pieces developed — used by bs_development_gap
fact_glossary.bs_back_rank_count: Count of user minor pieces still on starting back rank — used by bs_pieces_on_back_rank
fact_glossary.bs_king_square: User's king square — used by bs_king_* templates
fact_glossary.bs_missing_shield: Count of missing shield-pawn squares in front of king — used by bs_king_shield_broken
fact_glossary.bs_attacker_count: Count of distinct opp pieces attacking user's king zone — used by bs_king_attackers
fact_glossary.bs_user_central: Count of user attacks on central squares (e4/d4/e5/d5) — used by bs_central_control_gap
fact_glossary.bs_opp_central: Count of opp attacks on central squares — used by bs_central_control_gap
fact_glossary.bs_file_letter: File letter ('a'..'h') of an open file controlled by opp major — used by bs_open_file_owned_by_opp
fact_glossary.bs_opp_major_piece: Piece type ('rook' or 'queen') controlling the open file — used by bs_open_file_owned_by_opp
fact_glossary.bs_queen_square: User's queen square when she's the only active piece — used by bs_queen_alone_active
fact_glossary.bs_passive_count: Count of user non-pawn pieces still in own-side ranks — used by bs_passive_pieces_count

variants.user_winning_position: {played_san} is fine — you're still winning. {best_move_san} would have kept the pressure on.
variants.user_losing_position: {played_san} doesn't change much — you were already losing. {best_move_san} would have made the loss slower.
variants.why_user_missed_mate: {best_move_san} would have led to mate in {missed_tactic_ply} moves.
variants.why_user_missed_clearance_attack: {best_move_san} clears the line — your {missed_clearance_attacker_piece} comes through to attack {missed_clearance_attack_square}.
variants.why_user_missed_clearance_then_check: {best_move_san} opens the line — your {missed_clearance_then_check_piece} can then play {missed_clearance_then_check_follow_up_san} to chase the king on {missed_clearance_then_check_king_square}.
variants.why_user_missed_attack_with_tempo_full: {best_move_san} hits the {attack_with_tempo_piece} on {attack_with_tempo_square} with tempo. Your follow-up: {attack_with_tempo_follow_up_san}.
variants.why_user_missed_queen_capture_with_check: {best_move_san} captures the {queen_fork_secondary_piece} on {queen_fork_secondary_square} with check, winning material.
variants.why_user_missed_queen_fork: {best_move_san} forks the king on {queen_fork_king_square} and the undefended {queen_fork_secondary_piece} on {queen_fork_secondary_square}.
variants.why_user_missed_endgame_pawn_grab: {best_move_san} grabs the undefended pawn on {endgame_loose_pawn_square}. In the endgame, hunt undefended pawns with your active pieces.
variants.why_user_missed_endgame_pawn_attack: {best_move_san} attacks the undefended pawn on {endgame_loose_pawn_square} — your {endgame_loose_pawn_moving_piece} can grab it next move. In the endgame, hunt undefended pawns with your active pieces.
variants.why_user_position_already_losing_since_k: You were already in trouble since move {losing_since_move}. {best_move_san} only slows it — the problem started earlier.
variants.why_user_position_already_losing: You were already in trouble before this move. {best_move_san} only slows the loss.
variants.why_user_blocks_pawn_supports: {played_san} blocks your {blocked_pawn_file}-pawn — {best_move_san} would have supported your {blocked_pawn_would_support} pawn.
variants.why_user_missed_material: {best_move_san} wins material in the resulting line.
variants.why_user_attacks_played: After {opp_reply_san}, your {moving_piece_type} on {target_square} has no safe square.
variants.bs_isolated_attacker: Your {bs_piece} on {bs_square} is alone in opponent territory with no defender.
variants.bs_worst_placed_piece: Your {bs_piece} on {bs_square} has only {bs_legal_count} legal moves.
variants.bs_development_gap: Opponent has developed {bs_opp_developed} pieces; you've developed {bs_user_developed}.
variants.bs_pieces_on_back_rank: You still have {bs_back_rank_count} minor pieces on the back rank.
variants.bs_king_shield_broken: Your king on {bs_king_square} has lost {bs_missing_shield} of its pawn shelter.
variants.bs_king_attackers: {bs_attacker_count} opponent pieces are aimed at your king on {bs_king_square}.
variants.bs_central_control_gap: Opponent attacks the center {bs_opp_central} times; you attack it {bs_user_central}.
variants.bs_open_file_owned_by_opp: The {bs_file_letter}-file is open and opponent's {bs_opp_major_piece} controls it.
variants.bs_queen_alone_active: Your queen on {bs_queen_square} is the only piece doing anything.
variants.bs_connected_rooks_only_opp: Opponent's rooks are connected; yours aren't yet.
variants.bs_passive_pieces_count: {bs_passive_count} of your pieces are still on your side of the board.
variants.why_opp_punish_check: You can play {user_best_reply_san} with a forcing reply.
variants.why_opp_punish_default: You can play {user_best_reply_san} to punish it.
variants.why_opp_hanging: Their {piece_type} on {square} is now undefended — take it.
